wizard.hint: Write down what you know; leaving a field blank is better than inventing. This produces a brief for your research assistant.

mandate.ask: Start with action draft of science_requirement_brief to structure this into a requirement brief and show me the gaps; I will fill them and then commit to open the project.
mandate.intro: I am opening a new project. Here is the need, stated up front:

wizard.needQuestion: The research question is the one field required to build a mandate.
wizard.openHint: Spend two minutes saying what you want to study, before any work starts

ph.data: Dataset name, source, licence; write "none" if you have none
ph.deadline: e.g. submit by 2027-03, or "within six months"
ph.deliverables: Conference abstract / journal paper / preregistration / internal report
ph.domain: Biomedical / neuroscience / psychology / economics / computer science
ph.equipment: Instruments, compute, software; write "ordinary workstation" if nothing special
ph.ethics: Approval id if you have one; otherwise the committee you plan to use
ph.license: Data use agreement or authorisation; name the licence for public data
ph.people: e.g. just me, with help on statistics
ph.question: e.g. In community adults over 60, tai chi three times weekly versus usual care, on falls over six months
ph.subjects: Population, where from, roughly how many

wizard.title: State the research need

hintField.question: One sentence: in which population, what compared with what, affecting what, over how long.

check.intro: First make sure the whole stack is actually up. If the five items below are all right, you can continue.

model.foot: Each provider key is the billing entity; the bill lives in the relay, and this page only reports on the same basis.
model.intro: The model and its key decide what you can do and who gets billed.
model.noKeys: No credential source found yet. The launcher injects keys through environment variables, or fill them in under Settings → Model.

project.intro: A project = one story you can finish. Give it a title first; the field and target journal can change later.
project.journalPh: Target journal (optional, e.g. Nature Human Behaviour)
project.titlePh: Title, e.g. dose-response of sleep duration on working memory

rules.intro: Twelve workflows and 55 gates. Remember three things and you can start:
rules.notice: You can reopen this guide anytime: Settings → Research Workbench → Reopen the onboarding guide.
rules.one: Every claim must be pointable in the source — an assertion without a citation is a blocker, not close enough.
rules.three: A stage not passing means a gate is closed, not that the model is lazy: open Stages to see which gate it is, and it will tell you what to add.
rules.two: Data, code, figures and environment fingerprints are all recorded; a rerun must reproduce the same figure.

session.errorGeneric: Session did not start: the UI only says new session failed; the real reason is in Settings → Research → preset diagnostics (/presets/inspect)
session.errorKeyMissing: Session did not start: the model key is not configured (Settings → Model). Configure it and click again.
session.errorNoPath: There is no existing workspace and no project directory, so a workspace cannot be created
session.errorNoUi: This shell has no uiWorkspace service, so a session cannot be started
session.intro: Pick one and click Start a session with this: the session is created with the prompt already in the input — press Enter to run.
session.startedDetail: Session started and the prompt is in the input box; press Enter to run.

sources.foot: After saving, close the panel to return here, then click Next.
sources.intro: Literature / search APIs: {ready}/{total} configured. All are optional — the public pool works without them.
sources.keys: Semantic Scholar / CORE / Zotero / Exa: more reliable with a key, usable without one.
sources.polite: OpenAlex / Unpaywall / Crossref: just add an email to join the polite pool — the three easiest ones.
sources.secrets: Keys are written only to the local science/config.json — never uploaded or echoed back.

hypothesis.text: Turn "<phenomenon>" into a testable hypothesis: H1 must state the independent variable, dependent variable and expected direction; use science_exp_plan for the smallest reproducible sample size and procedure, science_statistics_choice for the primary model, and list the preregistration points.

map.text: Build a literature map around "<research question>": use science_lit_query to pull the 15 core papers and science_gap_matrix to mark uncovered gaps; every conclusion must give its source, evidence strength, and reproducibility.

topic.text: I am working on "<direction>". Start with science_frontier_scan to map frontier anchors from the last two years, then use science_novelty to score three candidate topics for novelty, and finally tell me only which one is worth a paper and why.

net.unreachable: Cannot reach the local service; make sure the instance is still running.

pill.title: Today's token usage only; amounts and details live on the Billing page, with the relay as source of truth.
